summary: This edition covers the seven most recent days of Miqyas data, but they are not seven consecutive days: the crawl recorded Oct 24 to Oct 29 and then Nov 3, with no entries for Oct 30 to Nov 2. Six of these days also fell inside last week's roundup, so most of what follows is a second look at the same stretch, with Nov 3 the only new day. Across the 65 articles, social coverage again carried the heaviest negative weight: 22 of 65 social readings (34%) were negative, against 17% for political and 14% for economic. Those social negatives came largely from crime and safety reporting rather than politics: a judicial commission calling the police inquiry into the killing of Karachi businessman Mir Raza Ali an "epic failure", the family of Hina Javed asking Punjab's chief minister for a judicial probe into her death, harassment cases in Lahore and Karachi, a bus crash in Hafizabad, and an oxygen cylinder blast at a Tharparkar health centre that killed eight people.

The dominant storyline was the standoff between PTI and the state, the subject of five of the eleven flagged articles. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and Speaker Babar Saleem Swati were being held under house arrest and suggested the Oct 11 emergency could run past six months; three days later a Peshawar anti-terrorism court issued arrest warrants for Afridi and four other PTI leaders in the May 2023 Radio Pakistan attack case, which PTI disputes. Inside the party, most senators and MNAs at a seven-hour joint meeting argued against further talks with the establishment, while PTI publicly denied that its core committee had been sidelined. Imran Khan's sister Noreen Niazi was moved from jail to a cardiology hospital as Punjab extended the detention of Khan's three sisters by 30 days. Close to this thread, Lahore High Court judge Mohsin Akhtar Kayani resigned, citing health and his view that the 26th and 27th amendments have eroded high court independence. The other major thread was the Afghan border: Pakistan said it destroyed Afghan Taliban posts after fire from the Afghan side killed a civilian at Angoor Adda, then dismissed the Afghan Taliban's account as fabricated and alleged Indian involvement, claims that were not independently verified.

Political lean held steady despite this charged mix: 60 of 65 articles read balanced, five pro-government and none pro-opposition. The pro-government readings track sourcing, not a position Miqyas takes. Each was a story built on one side's uncontested account, such as a provincial government statement on housing schemes, a PM aide's claim of 'off-the-record' contacts with PTI with no PTI response, the information ministry's rebuttal of the Afghan Taliban, and, on Nov 3, a minister's description of the electoral reforms panel with no PPP or MQM reply. AI confidence was mostly medium (39 articles), with 24 high and only two low. Both low readings went to reports of militant commanders killed in Balochistan operations, the two stories where the reporting rested entirely on unnamed security sources with no independent confirmation.

Economic coverage stayed the calmest category, at about 82% neutral, and none of the flagged stories was primarily economic. Its negatives tracked prices and trade: a sharply wider regional trade deficit, higher customs values on imported stationery raw materials, a scrapped vaccine tender, diesel nearing Rs400 a litre on Oct 29, and, on Nov 3, traders and millers saying imported wheat had failed to bring flour prices down. Nov 3 also brought the clearest economic positive in the window, a cut of Rs7.76 per litre in high-speed diesel and Rs3.40 in petrol, following two late-October increases in the diesel rate. The one flagged item that day was procedural: the Election Commission said it is ready to hold Islamabad's local government polls on Dec 20 under the 2015 law, because Parliament ended its sessions without passing the bill for new town corporations.

notableStories.headline: KP Governor Kundi says Sohail Afridi, assembly speaker 'in safe hands' after house arrest
notableStories.context: The governor confirmed that KP's elected chief minister and assembly speaker were being held under house arrest and suggested the emergency and governor's rule could run past six months, while relatives of both men petitioned the Peshawar High Court.

notableStories.headline: Justice Kayani resigns, citing growing control over the judiciary
notableStories.context: A sitting Lahore High Court judge stepped down, saying the 26th and 27th amendments have eroded high court independence and widened executive influence on judicial appointments and transfers.

notableStories.headline: Pakistan strikes Afghan Taliban posts after cross-border attack
notableStories.context: According to local officials, fire from the Afghan side killed a civilian and wounded five members of a family at Angoor Adda, a border trade route, and security sources said Pakistani forces responded by destroying several Afghan Taliban posts.

notableStories.headline: ISI, IB officials included in JIT formed to probe Mir Raza murder
notableStories.context: After a judicial commission called the police inquiry into the killing of a Karachi businessman an "epic failure", the Sindh government brought intelligence agencies and the Rangers into a new joint investigation team.

notableStories.headline: ECP says ready to hold LG polls in ICT
notableStories.context: The Election Commission plans to hold Islamabad's local government elections on Dec 20 under the 2015 law because Parliament did not pass the bill for new town corporations, making months of delimitation work redundant.
